questions.q: Where does a data consumer find the Request access button for an asset?
options: Right on the asset's own details page, in the same menu as Edit and Delete
In a completely separate IT ticketing system outside of Purview
Only an administrator can submit requests, never the consumer themselves
It's emailed to the consumer automatically on a monthly schedule
questions.explain: Request access sits directly in the asset's own action menu alongside Edit, Refresh, and Delete — there's no separate system a consumer has to go learn.

questions.q: What action actually triggers the underlying self-service access workflow?
options: Selecting Send on the filled-out Request access form
Simply viewing the asset's details page
Searching for the asset in the catalog search bar
Scrolling to the bottom of the asset's schema tab
questions.explain: Finding and viewing the asset doesn't trigger anything by itself — Send is the action that fires the workflow and notifies the approver.

questions.q: What does an approved access request become afterward, according to this lesson?
options: A tracked record showing the data source path, access type, requestor, and date — an audit trail
Nothing — approved requests are deleted immediately with no record kept
A permanent, unchangeable grant that can never be revoked
A new Azure subscription created automatically for the requestor
questions.explain: The request becomes a tracked self-service access policy record, which is what lets a governance team audit who has access to what, and who approved it, later.

questions.q: In the request status lifecycle, what's the difference between Approved and Completed?
options: Approved means granted but not yet provisioned; Completed means the data asset has actually been provisioned for use
They are two names for the exact same status
Approved comes after Completed in the sequence
Completed means the request was denied
questions.explain: Approved and Completed are distinct states — a request can sit as Approved before the actual data access is provisioned, and only reaches Completed once that provisioning is done.

questions.q: What happens to a Pending request if the approver denies it?
options: It moves to Declined, ending that path
It automatically moves to Completed anyway
It loops back to Pending indefinitely until approved
It silently grants access without notifying anyone
questions.explain: A request can move from Pending to Declined (ending it) or from Pending to Approved and then Completed — it never skips a state or grants access after a denial.
